I was supposed to carry out other tasks, such as giving support to the corps artillery group, coordinated action, cooperation, communication between the units; whereas, they were supposed to deal autonomously with their axes and their zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document can be put away. I'm going to turn to another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, in your testimony yesterday, you discussed the order for Operation Uragan and explained how you had seen General Rasim Delic at Visoko, where the order, a map for Uragan was approved. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And I still stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can look at Exhibit 402, please. Now, General, we looked at this order yesterday. And forgive me if I'm asking you to repeat yourself, but it's right, isn't it, that this document was prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By me alone. Of course, I mean my command staff, not just I personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. And in the copy of the document that we have before us, if we can just go to the final page in the B/C/S, please. You told us yesterday that on this particular copy, it doesn't have your signature, but you believed that you would have signed the other, first copy, of this document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this exactly. I do remember that I brought along two copies and that it was in a hurry that the commander signed both copies. He signed the map at the same time. I don't recall whether Sakib Mahmuljin had the order at all. I know that his map was signed by the commander too. We briefly looked at the map, and that was when this particular activity was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Concentrating on the other copy, because you told us that you took along two copies. The other copy which General Delic approved, that did have your signature on it, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the other one. I believe the first one did. The second one might not have had. But don't hold me to that. I'm not sure. The first one should have had it, 100 per cent sure. I recall that it was in great haste and automatically that the commander signed both.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned that when you met with General Delic, you had the order and a map. Would you agree with me that under army standard procedure the order and the map would only contain information about the corps level and the unit immediately subordinate to the corps level?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. This is quite understandable, because geographic maps are of larger or smaller scale and, of course, not every single soldier could be plotted onto the map. There is a standard operational procedure for the corps command level where the division is very important. Its area of responsibility and its task. Possibly the positions can also be plotted into the map of the brigades, I mean, in order to know what the situation is. That's important for the corps commander, but otherwise the standard operational procedure does not require this to be in the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you provided the order and the map to General Delic, you had already decided which units the 2nd Corps would use; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this had been completed. I was there for the ammunition and for the explosives, for the most part. Yesterday I explained why we had the situation. There were two corps, great losses. The problem and the situation was becoming more and more complex given the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Exactly. You were the commander in the field. You knew the conditions, and therefore you were the appropriate person to decide which units to be used -- which subordinate units to be used within the operation.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when General Delic approved the plan -- sorry, the order and the map by placing his signature on it, this simply meant that the corps, the 2nd Corps, could proceed with the operation. That is right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meant to the Gloc commander, the grey-haired person we saw yesterday, as a signal to provide ammunition.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without that particular indication, he would not have provided any -- anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, it may be that the interpretation was lost there, so I'll repeat my question. When General Rasim Delic approved the order and the map by signing them, this simply meant that the 2nd Corps could proceed with Operation Uragan; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree by commenting in the following way: This approval to me was important in order to obtain materiel and technical equipment from Gloc, without which I would not have been able to do what I did. Had the conditions been different and had the 3rd Corps not been there, I -- I could not have carried this out without an approval.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness may have said "I could have carried this out without approval."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just intervene? The witness just said "I could have approved it -- I could have done it without approval," and it was entered "I could not have done it." Can the witness please clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can interrupt. Both of you are talking at the same time. Madam Vidovic, you were talking. The interpreter was talking. I don't know whether what you said was interpreted. Can we ask Mr. Robson to please ask the question again and let the interpreter interpret.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I'd just like to clarify that specific part of the answer, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By a question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, did you say - and again, please clarify if I have this wrong - "had the conditions been different and had the 3rd Corps not been there, I could have carried out this without approval"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. I didn't even have an entire corps. I had 5.000 and 100 or 200 attackers and two batches of brigades, around 2.000 of them. So it was on the basis of the directive and the instructions and guidelines that I received, I could have carried this out without a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And apart from deciding which units to use and planning the operation, it's correct that you actually named the operation as Uragan; is that so? Uragan 95.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get clarification, Mr. Robson. This answer as corrected makes it difficult for me to follow the logic of the argument, and I'll tell you why. Mr. Delic told us a couple of minutes ago that without General Delic's signature, the Gloc commander couldn't give him the materiel and equipment to go to war. Therefore, this seems to suggest to me that without the signature he could not go to war. Now, if he now says that -- if the correction now is: "So it was on the basis of the directive and the instructions and guidelines that I received I could have carried this out without a signature," then that doesn't make sense. How -- was he going to fight with his bare hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I clarify this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This particular signature has not much to do with Gloc, G-l-o-c. The commander of the General Staff does have the influence to order Halid Cengic, but I know that had the operation not been planned, he would not have issued a single bullet, because the situation was so difficult that it was very hard to get hold of materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess what I'm saying is, I don't understand how the operation could have been implemented without the approval of the general. As -- as you said, Mr. Delic, one, you didn't have arms and ammunition. If it is not approved, I don't know whether the 3rd Corps would have come to your rescue. I don't know whether without the 3rd Corps, would you have managed. You know, the whole operation for me seems to suggest that, from what I've heard you say so far -- seems to suggest that you needed to get his approval. But if I'm wrong, please say so. You don't have to explain. Just say, "No, you are wrong. I can -- I can go to war without his signature." That's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. You're wrong. What you have stated here is not what I wanted to say. I said that there were 9.000 men in all. If I had 50 or 60 thousand men at the time, this is not a corps. This is just a part of a corps. There was no reason for me, without the signature of the commander of the General Staff, Rasim Delic, not to carry out combat activities in my area of responsibility had the situation not been in the Vozuca theatre of war as it was, as I described yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, I'm going to put that issue to one side for the moment, and I'm going to turn briefly to the operative tactical analysis on the liberation of Vosica that we looked at yesterday. And this is Exhibit 407. I take it that you recognise this document, General?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. We commented upon it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And during your comments yesterday, you explained that this document was part of an -- an exercise to analyse all combat operations that took place during the war; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. This was no exercise. This was an operation. If this has been interpreted correctly, this was no exercise. This is an operations and tactical analysis within a project that lasted for two or two and a half years in order to make a record of what had been going on in the war. This was no exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Again, we're at cross-wires, general. By "exercise" what I meant was this analysis was part of a project. But -- but I think you've explained clearly what -- what the purpose was. Yesterday in your evidence, General, you -- you told us that you didn't think the project was very successful. And by this, I'm talking about the project to analyse the combat operations. And you explained some of the problems.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was my assessment. I don't believe it was ever completed satisfactorily. There are several reasons for it. Quite a long period of time elapsed. Some people retired. Others died. Some were demobilised. It was very difficult to obtain information. I believe the analysis was relatively good. The first part of it was a military analysis, because, of course, it had to do with a military operation. But for the rest, the analysis was, in my view, quite poor. Among other things, the army general Rasim Delic retired in that period of time, and I believe that his successor did not bring this to completion. There were quite a few shortcomings. There was exaggerations, boasting. Some titles of units were simply made up, and others that were in fact involved in the execution of these tasks were not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just bear with me a moment, please, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, would you agree that the results of the analysis into Operation Uragan were supposed to be verified by a special commission of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that some 15 holders of Ph.D. degrees were engaged on this and they were supposed to categorise the material, to check up on it, and to sort it out. Now, as for this operations and tactical analysis, I am sure that at least 90 per cent of the information contained therein is true, because I was there in charge of the analysis, as well as the division general. My answer to your question is affirmative. The objective was to show the relevant historical facts to the generations to come, in order for them to draw lessons for the -- for better or for worse on the basis of what had happened in those four years of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, if I suggest that the -- this analysis here was not verified by that special commission, would -- would you agree with me or would you disagree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you. I am not even sure that it ever reached them. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And so, General, you've set out quite a list of problems with the analysis that took place of these combat operations and agreed that this analysis was not verified by the special commission. Can I refer your attention to page 4 in the B/C/S document and page 6 of the English. Now, it's point 4 which I'm interested in. If you could just scroll down. General, before you answer any question, can I ask you this: Bearing in mind what you told us about the way that Uragan was planned and prepared by the 2nd Corps in accordance with the directive, it's not right to say, is it, that the carrying out of the combat activities was ordered by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't really agree with you. De facto the order and the map were approved. That is to say, they were signed. With the very fact they were signed and approved on the basis of the directive and guidelines, I took it to be a sufficient reason to place the army General Staff there; although, I myself, of course, did produce this on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And indeed, General, as you say, you produced it on your own and you've confirmed that General Delic simply gave his approval of the combat activities. And that's so, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something I've been stating all this time, both during proofing and in my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, I'd like to turn to the two coordination plans that you were shown yesterday. I'm just going to focus on one by way of example. If we could bring up Exhibit 399, please. General, could you confirm that what we can see here is the coordination plan for August 1995? And it bears the date of the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, General, I don't want you to -- to repeat yourself too much, but could you briefly explain again what this document is.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is - at least, I see it that way - an arbitrary plan regulating the life and work in the units for the months to come. It lists some main activities and several headlines, activities, the persons to carry them out, time frames, and some remarks. It was made in order to provide an orientation as to what had to be done in the months to come and within what time frames.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General. And if I understood your evidence correctly, the way that this coordination plan would be prepared is that every month a corps would make its own coordination plan and then forward that coordination plan on to the staff of Hadzihasanovic, the chief of staff. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something I stated yesterday in those two documents - and there's another one - that most probably this was an expert -- excerpt from my plan of activities for the forthcoming months. Both those plans were produced, because a staff communicates with a staff horizontally and provides them with information. Probably they compiled the information received into a collection or summary of plans. This is something that can be seen in our documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So they compiled it. They put it into one document. And that's what we can see on the screen in front of us.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. I believe that that was the whole purpose of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's correct to say, isn't it, that this coordination plan was not considered to be a combat document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was never a combat document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can look at this August plan and see what the tasks are in here relating to the 2nd Corps. If we can please look at page 14 of the English document, page 12 of the B/C/S. General, I believe it's under Roman numeral 13, the tasks for the 2nd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can just look at some of the items set out in this coordination plan. If we can scroll down a page, please, in the -- in the B/C/S version. Would you agree with me that item 2 relates to accommodation?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we turn to the next pages in both documents, please. And if we can look at item 5, so if we can scroll up in the English version, please and ... Is it right that item 5 here relates to training of officers of the 2nd Corps command?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is stated here that this is the training of officers of the 2nd Corps and that the time frame was probably 30th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And then perhaps just the last item we'll look for the 2nd Corps is item number 7. Is it right that this task concerns the renovation of existing and the building of new wooden facilities for the units?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was my task, because there had been a transformation of the 28th Division, the 24th and the 25th Divisions were merged, and those were my personal plans as to how to solve the problem, which was the accommodation of these units, as I've already told you. I told you yesterday. And the reappointment of the commands, that's also one of the things that these -- this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So would you agree with me, General, that this plan that we see here before, and the other examples that we -- exist, they have nothing to do with the coordination of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This arises from the fact that this was not a combat document. This was my regulation of the life and work in the units and dealing with certain problems there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'd like to turn to the ways that you discussed yesterday that the 2nd and 3rd Corps commanders concretely coordinated their combat activities. And if we could bring up Exhibit 403, please. Now, General, you discussed this document yesterday when you were questioned by the Prosecutor. Do you agree this is an order from you dated the 1st of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that from the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that you issued this order with the intention of carrying out concrete coordination of combat activities between the 2nd and 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, I have to explain. During that period of time, all the documents had already been prepared; all the combat documents, that is, on both sides. They were in -- towards the end of the preparation in the divisions and the brigades. Some of the obligations that were on the part of the -- of officers and commands were being realised towards the end of the planning of the combat activities. And this is precisely what is being regulated by this document. A team consisting of the most responsible people goes to the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps in order to concretely coordinate combat activities, which means cooperation between the units that are involved in combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just to -- to recap briefly, General, you told us that the purpose of these meetings was to discuss issues such as to decide which targets to fire on.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: To --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which means targets, the contact lines, the way of marking the area, how far the units of the 3rd Corps can go, how far can mine go, division of artillery targets so as to -- not to waste ammunition, the establishment of links, links between corps and divisions, looking at the terrain from the other side, meaning reconnoitering; and all the other important issues of significance for combat operations that were to expect -- to be expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So the reality is, General, that the coordination of Farz and Uragan took place in the field, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It follows from that that the General Staff did not coordinate the activities of the 2nd and 3rd Corps during Farz and Uragan. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no single officer there. Later on, Mr. General Enver Hadzihasanovic was sent there, but as far as I can remember, he was just a transmission from the logistics commander to receive equipment for further offensive activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, General, bear with me a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, we know that General Hadzihasanovic was in the area, because we saw him on the video yesterday. But can we just be clear he did not -- I apologise. I withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not in my area. I saw him only once or twice in the area of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, the point that I need to clarify with you: It's right to say, isn't it, that General Hadzihasanovic had nothing to do with the coordination taking place between the 2nd and 3rd Corps during the operations?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, in connection with Operation Uragan, I'd like to turn to another exhibit, if I may. It's a -- it's P2498. It may have been admitted as an exhibit. I'll just double-check. P2498, please. If we could just scroll to the bottom of the B/C/S version, please, and if we can just go to page 2 in the English, just to establish who the document is from.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom of this document, you can see that this is my document, this is my signature. Because of the change in the situation, a new order was issued for further combat operations; i.e., the engagement of the units in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could just scroll back up in the B/C/S version, go back to the page 1 in the English. Can you tell us a little bit more, General, about this order?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I can. I can read everything; because I can't remember everything off the top of my head. This is a supplement order -- of deploying units for immediate, next and subsequent tasks. Sent to the command of the 2nd Division of the army, section -- let me not go through that. I don't think it's necessary. The 1978 edition. Under 4: "I have decided the following: With the main forces, upon linking up with the forces of the BH army's 3rd Corps, on the line: Vissic, trig point 497, Djurica Vis, trig point 505."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General. There's no need to read the order out. But perhaps you could just confirm for us: That from this order, is it right that you are deciding and ordering new activities for the divisions, the 22nd Division?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only for them. For all the divisions. For the entire 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And also in this order, we can see that you are specifying the combat formation to be used as well.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here what is defined is that in this task, they have to form attack force, the defence line and the support or reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And what this order shows is that you were commanding the subordinate units and that you didn't need the approval from the General Staff in order to issue these new assignments; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday: I said that I was personally in command of all divisions and that I was on the forward line of the entire defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General. And if I could show you a final document before we break again. It's P2571. 2571.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I neglected to ask for that document to be entered -- to be tendered into evidence. Please could it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May P2498 please be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 420.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, it doesn't appear to be the correct document. I asked for P2571. It -- it may be that I've made the mistake. Your Honours, it appears that perhaps we have our numbers slightly out of order. Could -- is it possible to take a break now and we'll deal with it on our return?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. That will give you time to sort yourselves out. We'll take a break and come back to quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, before you continue, just one little question. And let me preface my question by saying it is not the intention of the Chamber to interfere with your cross-examination. But having said that, the Chamber sees a particular thrust - it's one, you may have many - that the Defence is going into. Do you -- do you think you need to go through all these documents one by one to make that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm well aware that it's probably not been the most interesting of afternoons for the Bench. But please, it -- if I can just say that we are well aware of the Prosecution's case from the indictment, and we have spent a lot of time looking at the PTs and the documents and exhibits which may well come into evidence and have already come into evidence. And the position is that a lot of the questions we've been putting today are really dealing with broader issues, because this is really the only opportunity we're going to get to -- to get a commander of a -- a corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand. But as I'm saying, I understand that. All I'm saying is, we can see a particular direction. And at least I'm of the view that you can -- you could make that point in one paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I mean, what I can tell you is that I'm drawing to the -- the conclusion of my issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: There's one which I will need to deal with in some length.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: But if we can return to the document that we were trying to bring up before the break. It's P2731.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did we do with 2571?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was our fault. It was an incorrect number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So we cancelled 2571?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, General, the document you have in front of you. If we could just quickly turn to the last page of the B/C/S version so we can establish who this is from. Do you see the name there, General?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was my then-assistant for morale, guidance and political issues, doctor of science, Salih Kulenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: He's a member of the 2nd Corps, then, is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in the command of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can we turn back to the front page, please, in the B/C/S version. Is this document headed with the words "Preparations and the state of combat morale in the Operation Uragan 95"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before, General?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If you could just very briefly -- and not read out loud, but if you could just to yourself very briefly read the first few parts of this document that you can see on the page in front of you.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read the first passage already.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to say, does this document summarise the steps that the commanding staff for morale took during Operation Uragan?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's only one of the parts of that organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can please turn to page 3 in the English version and page 2 in the B/C/S. There's a particular paragraph I'd just like to ask you about, General. Now, if you could look at the paragraph that starts halfway down the page. And in the English version, again, it's the middle section we're interested in. General, do you see some text which begins: "Shortcomings and flaws in the organisation were particularly obvious, which especially negatively affected the spirit and combat motivation of the troops"? Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I must admit that I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So if you start at the halfway point, General, and look at the text below that, do you see reference there to -- I don't think it's possible to close in any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Counsel, can it be highlighted in yellow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that possibility, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, first of all, General, can you read the text as posed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. And I'll try. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is reading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "There is the lack of synchronisation of units and -- between the army and civilian authorities. Shortcomings and flaws in the organisation were particularly obvious, which especially negatively affected the spirit and combat motivation of the troops. The dissonance was rather prevalent during the collection of the booty. There were many loose cannons present, which had affected the combat readiness and overall success that could have been achieved in the final liberation of the area of Ozren."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General. What I'd like to ask you about is the sentence which says "there were many loose cannons present, which had affected the combat readiness and overall success that could have been achieved in the final liberation of the area of Ozren." Can you help us? Do you know what this sentence means?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that I know; although, it is very delicate to explain what it means. The civilian authorities in the municipalities of Lukavac and Zavidovici did not undertake adequate measures in order to secure the newly liberated territories. There were a lot of things, such as looting certain houses, breaking and entering without consent, which presented lots of problems to the army. On top of our normal activities, we had to dedicate some troops to control the territory, because we were afraid of the infiltrated groups. We had handed over the terrain to the municipalities of Zavidovici and Lukavac and they were supposed to, in their capacities as civilian authorities, together with the civilian police, to organise unhindered life and activities there, but they failed to do that, and I suppose that this part refers to what I've just told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General. I'm going to move on to -- sorry, please could this be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 421.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'm going to turn to the issue of the intercept that we saw yesterday. It's Exhibit 414. Could the document please be brought up on screen. Now, General, I'm right in saying you told us that you didn't personally receive this document at any point, did you?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you described this transcript as raw material. It sets down the way that it was taped by those officers. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, can you confirm --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a group of soldiers which was monitoring and was recording what was happening in real life without any comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: For those soldiers who were carrying out the monitoring, does it follow that the three speakers that appear on this transcript must have been speaking the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. You can see it in here. That's how it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can just quickly turn to page 2 in both documents, please. I say it's page -- I've referred to page 2 in the B/C/S. It may not be; it may be on the first page. General, do you see the -- thank you. If we can leave the English version on the second page, as it is. General, can you see the exchange where a person marked as "Y" says, "Who am I speaking to?" And the person marked as "M" responds, "With the Mujahedin commander." Do you see that in your version?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have a different page 2. Can we have page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see it now, General? It's about the middle --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document, and I'm trying to find that section. Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So the exchange that I'm interested in is that a person who's marked as "Y" says, "Who am I speaking to?" And then a person marked as "M" says, "With the Mujahedin commander." It should be in the bottom quarter of the screen, General.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With the commander of the Mujahids." Therefore, not Mujahedins -- Mujahedin, but Mujahid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Ah. Could you explain the difference for us, General, between "Mujahids" and "Mujahedin"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to explain that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: But there is a distinction, is there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just bear with me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The question that I was -- I wanted to ask you, General, was that: Would you agree with me the reason why the person marked as "M" has been identified as a Mujahid or Mujahedin is because of this comment he makes, where he says: "With the Mujahedin commander"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that's the case. But somebody from the 3rd Corps would be able to tell you something more specific about it. Although, I do believe that "M" is connected with "Mujahid." Of course, provided that this is somebody from the 3rd Corps. I don't really know who this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. General, can you just confirm that this text does not say, "With the Mujahedin commander." That is not the correct translation of what that person said.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just as we don't know what delta X or delta Y stands for. These are code names for the persons using the communications device. These are not the precise names of the participants but, rather, the code names of the participants in the radio communication. Every radio set and each participant have their code names.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just to -- just to clarify, General, what did that person say if he didn't say, "With the Mujahedin commander"? What is the correct -- what are the correct words used? Would you read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said not "with the commander" but, rather, "with the komandir. " A "komandir" is the person in charge of a smaller unit, a squad, a platoon, or company. The term "commander" is used for the battalion level and above, division, brigade, and so on. If he says "komandir," this means that he's in command of a smaller unit. It can be a squad. It may be a platoon or a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that, General, but what I was trying to get at is could you just read the entire sentence out, what this person actually said.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sentence reads: "With the komandir of the Mujahids."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And -- okay. Thank you, General. I'm going to move away from this issue and -- and come back to the order that was disputed yesterday, which was the Exhibit MFI 415. Now, yesterday, General, you confirmed that you never saw this order before attending at this hearing. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I gave it a bit of thought, and I believe that this order was drafted by the late General Mustafa Hajrulahovic and that this is not a document of the General Staff but, rather, as it is stated in the heading, it's a document of the administration for intelligence and security. It wasn't referenced in a file. I didn't see it. But it doesn't mean that it never reached my office. This can be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Did the question -- or what I was asking you to confirm, General, is you never saw this order, did you, prior to attending this hearing?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you told us that the document did not seem right to you. First of all, you mentioned that there was no strictly confidential number on it. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It's also true that under "3"- and this is something I thought about yesterday - what is referred to is Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan, and he was the head of the administration for intelligence. I believe that he wrote it without his knowledge and that he was not able to receive a reference number because he did not receive the approval of the commander. I think that we can check this in the files. This isn't an original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we -- could we see paragraph 3 of the English version, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Concerning Mustafa Hajrulahovic, it's the case, isn't it, that that gentleman is now deceased? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I wouldn't want to discuss him at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So there's no way for us to check whether or not he was involved in the preparation of this order. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He must have taken part in this, because otherwise his name would not be there at the bottom. What is disputable - and this can be checked in the archives of the corps or of this particular administration, although, as we see, there is no reference number - he may have tried to do this on his own, of his own accord.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: He may have tried to do this on his own. You're speculating, aren't you, General, as to what this order may be or how it may come about.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person is deceased, and please accept my position that I don't want to comment upon him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the other factors which led you to believe that this document didn't seem right. You said there was a contradiction because the document came from an administration when it was -- when it's purported to come from the commander. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two major issues that are contradictory here: The first one being that nowhere in the heading in the upper left-hand corner does it state that the document is filed, because there is no reference number. This is one inconsistency. The second inconsistency is that it is not stated where it was sent. First, a document should have the name of the author who drafted it, and then to whom it was addressed. This is copy number 1, which means that this is the administration copy, and it was not filed in the administration, which means that there's something irregular about it. This was a copy that was supposed to be kept in the place where it was drafted. As such, it could not have been sent anywhere. Therefore, it had -- it has to be an original.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have to be an original.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, General, that there's a further contradiction? Because this document appears on the face of it to have originated in the administration for intelligence and security, but if we look at who it's addressed, to it simply states it's to the 2nd Corps and to the 7th Motorised Brigade. If this had been a legitimate document, this document would have been addressed to the administrations of both of those units; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that you are quite familiar with the military hierarchy of our organisation. It is not normal for the administration to send to the command of the 2nd Corps anything. Under the structure, it could only have communicated something to the administration of the same department or to its own counterpart.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And something else that's strange about this document, General: If we could look at point number 1, it's talking about members of the former El Mujahid unit. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. That's item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And yet this document is being sent to the command of the 2nd Corps. Now, to your knowledge, were there any members of the El Mujahid Detachment living in Tuzla either during or after the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that based upon all of these contradictions that we've discussed today, that this order may well have been prepared by someone that doesn't understand the ARBiH very well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could put it that way. There are quite a few contradictions. You have to keep in mind that this was after the war; that this detachment did not operate as a detachment. They had been disbanded. I don't know what the objective was, because I or my subordinates never contacted them directly. Particularly not in the post-war period when the Army of the Federation was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Precisely so. And then if we can look at -- or discuss one final matter, which is rather strange about this document. If we can scroll back to the top of the B/C/S version. General, would you agree with me that it -- this document purports to have been sent by the packet system?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, that it was transmitted by packet. I don't know what was used, in fact, to transmit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, what I'd like to do is show you a different document - two documents, in fact - to show what we could expect if the document had been sent by packet. So if we could please bring Exhibit 375 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the identification of the likes of me. Could we also get, if the witness is able to, an explanation of what a packet system is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Exactly. That's what I was going to do next, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what the packet communication system was or is.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a device which was introduced, I believe, in late 1994 or in 1995, which made possible fast transmission of communications; namely, orders, and any other sort of communication between two participants. To put it briefly, this is a device whereby all these documents were sent and on the basis of which a communication link was set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General. And perhaps just for us to explain a little further, if we can look at page 5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me. It is not quite clear whether the transmission was electronic or physical.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Electronic. Electronic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So if we could please bring up page 5 in the English version and -- it's the last page in the B/C/S, which is page 4. If we could please try and reduce the document down so we can try and have it all on -- on one page. Okay. That's -- that's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, General, I'm not bothered particularly about the content of what this document says. I'm more interested in the form of it. Would you agree with me what -- what this is is a -- is a document and we can see at the bottom that somebody has signed for the commander Rasim Delic? If we can scroll down in the English page, please.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that somebody has prepared a physical document, a piece of paper in this instance, and somebody has put a stamp on this document and a signature, signing it for Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says here, "for," and then there are the initials of the person. They are in the lower left-hand corner, "MM." So the person doing the encryption received the document at such-and-such an hour on the 22nd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Pause there, please, General. So having told us that we've started off with a physical document which has a stamp and a signature, would you agree with me that we can tell from this document that the contents of this document were sent using the packet communication system?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. This is similar to the facsimile we have today. I don't know how else I should explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And am I right in saying that in this instance the reason we can tell that this document was sent using the packet system is because of the handwritten information in the bottom left-hand corner of the document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're right. To say the least, it is quite strange that it is not placed in one's own hand, in spite of the stamp. If this is an original, then it should read that it was personally signed by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: As I say, General Delic, it's -- the content is not so important. We're trying to look at the procedure by which documents were sent by packet. And would you -- would you agree with me that the handwritten information in the bottom left-hand corner indicates that this document was sent using the packet system at 14.48 hours on the 22nd of July, 1995? And then underneath that, we can see that somebody has signed --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Put a signature to it saying that that has been done.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, before we leave this document, one final thing I'd like to mention: You would agree with me that looking at the format of this document, it looks as though it's been prepared on maybe a typewriter or a -- a word processor or something like that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to the -- the pages before. So it's going to be page 4 in the English, page 3 in the B/C/S. Sorry, the English is on two pages, so if we can go to the page before, just -- in the English version. Now, first of all, General, I know -- I said the -- the contents of the other document was not important, but would you agree with me that what we can see there is the text that was contained in that last document? It's been transferred into a different format.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to take a look at the text first. Yes, yes. Well, if you're referring to the form of sending the document and all that, I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So just to explain the process or perhaps you could do this for us, General, it's right that from taking an original document with a stamp and a signature, we then move to this sort of document here. And this is the thing which is actually transmitted via the packet communication system. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can look at the top of this page, we can see that there's a solid line that runs horizontally, and above that there's some information. Can you tell us what that means and what sort of information is contained there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the top left-hand corner, it reads: "The administration of the Military Security Service," and the date is the 22nd of July, 1995. "Day: Saturday." In the middle, it says: "Sarajevo, encryption" -- or rather,"the General Staff, encryption, hours: 1520." In the top right-hand corner, it reads: "Original file. Document received." And next to that there is a signature. Following the words "original file," there are some letters I can't make out. And below, it says: "Document received by," and then there's the signature of a person, which is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: From this document, General, are we able to tell whether this is what has been received from the far end, if you like, of the packet communication system or is this the document that entered into the packet communication system? Can we tell that from the information at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the original from the packet communication. I said yesterday that the previous document was highly suspicious. It should have quite a different appearance. Again, you're prompting me to give my opinion of a person who is deceased, and it's always easy to lay the blame on him. I believe that for some reason this was done by the late General Talijan Hajrulahovic and that he sent this without the knowledge --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: With respect, General, I'm going to ask you not to speculate on how that document may have arisen, but what I will ask you is that: If that document had been sent via the packet system, we could have expected to see it either in this sort of format and certainly bearing the sort of signatures, the types of signatures and the types of information that we can see on this page. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. This question should have been put at the outset, and I believe that any additional discussion is superfluous. So I think that, of course, it has to have the heading saying who sent it and then who received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to turn to my final issue, and I'll leave this open to you to explore if you wish to find out more about the packet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll ask maybe one or two questions just about the packet. You know, and I -- and I must concede up front that my knowledge of technology is very limited. Now, from my knowledge of technology, the technology that sends documents fast recently is a fax, and before the fax it was the telex. Is there anything else? Is a packet none of these two?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could put that to the witness, if he -- if he's able to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The packet -- Mr. Delic, is the packet communication neither a telex nor a fax? Do you remember a telex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it's more similar to telex. What puzzles me is the heading here. I even find the bottom section of the document in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The important issue is that nobody received the document and nobody filed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Forget about the appearance of the document. I just wanted to find out. Is a packet communication something other than a telex? Then we move on because as you speak, that's what I'm trying to imagine what could have been used, and I'm not able to come up with any answer. This was not a telex, a packet communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was something similar to that. I said that it was something similar, technically speaking, but not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, it could not have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just finally on this issue, can you confirm, General, that in sending information via the packet communication system it was not like a fax machine; it could not record a signature or a stamp. It would only pass the hard physical typeface that we see on the document in front of us?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: All right. The final issue, General, relates to that of reporting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm getting a little confused. You say -- I thought you have been saying to the witness that these documents that have the signature either of General Delic or somebody signing on his behalf are documents that went through the packet system. Now, when you say "just finally on this issue, can you confirm, General, that in sending information via the packet communication system it was not like a fax machine; it could not record a signature or a stamp," then I get confused, because it sounds like you have been contradicting what you have been saying all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if perhaps I could put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But is that what you have said?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, just read -- read your question on the screen and tell me what -- whether that's what you had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm talking about the physical delivery of the document. The signatures that we have -- that we can see on this document here, what I've been -- what I'd hoped to ascertain from the witness is that this was part of the process by which the document was sent. So the document either going in or the document going out, somebody could indicate that the document had been sent, but those signatures would not be transmitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Like a fax, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I guess the real issue is, if a signature could be transmitted through the packet system. So if the sending document had a signature, would that signature then be visible in the receiving document, in the receiving end.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if the witness could deal with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You couldn't see the signature. The packet communication is -- how can I explain it? First, you have to encrypt or code by means of equipment. You change the form of the words. For example, if you want to put the heading "Information," it wouldn't appear in the Bosnian language as "information." It would appear as a coded, protected message. And as such, when this is typed, you cannot decode it if the other participant in the communication does not have a similar equipment to use for the decoding. Every packet communication has to have the heading, the time of sending. The signature itself is not in dispute, although it may be, because we are talking about the original here. If there is an original, then -- if this is an original, then it wasn't sent with package communication. In the original, there shouldn't be a situation where the signature is lacking. In package communication, there should be a number. There doesn't have to be a signature, but there must be a number. As far as I can see, this is example number 1 from the headquarters or the bases that was sent, not that arrived at my office, because it is indicated that it was sent to the 7th Brigade. It is the original example from the base where it was created. In other words, it had to have both the signature, the stamp, and it had to be registered. And all that I was talking about boiled down to that. I don't know how else I can explain to you that there are two pieces of equipment, on two sides, and these two pieces of equipment are compatible. They can communicate to each other. And those who are trying to intercept that conversation in -- in the air, they cannot understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clears a lot of air. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The final point on this, General: So the document is sent via the packet system. It is received at one -- at the far end. And what comes out is a document such as -- like we can see on the screen, except it will have no -- obviously no written signatures or written -- handwritten information on it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. What you receive is a document similar to this one with the heading which shows when it was sent, where it was sent, who registered it. Every piece of equipment will register that unless the document is an original, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So in the top part above the horizontal line, we have the information about when it was received, the date, and also we can see a serial number as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But we have explained everything. It is precisely as you are now saying. The top part is actually the information about the time when the piece of equipment received this communication. And you can see the time, 15.20. There should be also a signature of the person who received it, but it's missing. But the time is here, when it was received.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General. I'll try and deal with this last issue very quickly. Is it right that in the 2nd Corps command there was an operation centre which received daily reports from subordinate levels below the corps?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All units in the direct line of communication with the corps would send once or twice a day daily reports, according to my scheme. They would send it to the operations centre. There those documents were processed. And then the interested parties would be informed about their contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that when those reports from the subordinate level arrived in the operations centre, an officer or a team of officers would review those reports and prepare one summary report? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. But if you will allow me a minute, I believe I can make your job easier. The battalion, as a lower unit in the brigade, sends its reports to the brigade -- the brigade, describing what happened in the battalion. Then the brigade reduces all these reports and sends their report to the division. The division, in it's turn, reduces the report, informs the corps, and then the corps considers that and decides what should be sent to the higher rulers. For example, the piece of information that should be three or four pages long is finally reduced to maybe half a page or one page. I know what you're aiming at, and I believe that I may -- I've been able to make your job easier and that I've saved you some time with this explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I believe you're correct. Could we please look at document D413. Now, General, can you tell from this document, is this a daily combat report from the 2nd Corps command dated the 11th of September, 1995 to the General Staff at Kakanj and some other places listed as well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we could just on the -- on the Bosnian version, if we could please look at page 2. We can see that there's a different piece of information there. And if we could look at page 3 now, as well. So if we can return to page 1. General, the question that I have is: Is it right that this document from the 2nd Corps to the General Staff at Kakanj deals with different issues? It talks of the aggressor. It gives information about combat activities, morale, and security.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. It is not correct for this reason: This was sent from the command post of the 2nd Corps in Cubric. Not from the command of the 2nd Corps. You can see that it was also sent to the operations centre which means that we were in a very specific situation and we were sending reports to those in Tuzla and we were some 20 kilometres or 30 kilometres from Tuzla. And as for the rest of your question, the answer is "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So among other places, this document, you agree, was sent to the General Staff at Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the General Staff command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could look at document P2588, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want to deal with D413?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could admit this into evidence. I was going to ask that they all be admitted at the same time. But if we could do it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 422.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we're waiting for the document to appear, P2588 is a document from the operation planning administration at KM Kakanj to the Presidency, the commander of the ARBiH, the Visoko Gloc, and the administration for morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: General, would you agree with me that in the top part of this document, it's dated the 12th of September, 1995 and it refers to the situation on the BiH battlefield for the 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could quickly scroll down through the -- the B/C/S version. If it could please be moved over to the right so the General can perhaps see a little bit more of the contents. If we can move -- Would you agree, General, first of all, on this page that we can see, that there are -- there is a summary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And can we lift the English as well, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: There is a summary about the activities of the enemy that deals with all of the different corps?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, that's right. This is a summary description of the situation on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And so would you agree with me that from the document that we saw a moment ago from the 2nd Corps dated the 11th of September, which was three pages in length, that -- the information in that document has been condensed and summarised within this document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that. That's how this was done. Sometimes it can happen for five or ten times. For example, for the 4th Corps, it says: "Movements of motor vehicle were noticed." I'm sure that a lot more information had arrived from the 4th Corps about the morale, the troops, the situation, but only one sentence was incorporated into the final report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In respect of the 2nd Corps, we can see that the information in that earlier report has been condensed to some three or four sentences; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten times.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than ten times.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, General. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you have --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry. If that document could please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 423.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a few questions on one issue arising from cross. Could the document Exhibit 415 Marked for Identification please be put back up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: While that's being done, General Delic, a few moments ago my learned colleague - and this is reflected on lines 18 to 22 of page 76 - asked you if there were any members of the El Mujahid Detachment living in Tuzla either during or after the war. And you answered: "No, never." Now, I'd like to ask you, sir: In November 1997, what was the area of responsibility that your corps covered?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I can't tell you off my head. There had been a reorganisation of the military, and I believe that at that period of time the 3rd Corps stopped existing, together with some other units, and I believe that the 2nd Corps remained together with the 1st and the 5th Corps. The only corps that existed as professional army, part of the territory of the 3rd Corps during the peacetime, although there was no special zone of responsibility, but some of the war units that continued that tradition and lived as war units within their command, they were in Tesanj, Zavidovici -- in Tesanj and in Zavidovici. In the municipality of Tuzla and the Tuzla canton, I don't know that there was a single member of the Mujahedin of whom you are now talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And -- and your answer, sir, is: "In the municipality of Tuzla and the Tuzla canton." Do you know if there were any former members of the Mujahedin detachment living in other areas covered by the 2nd Corps in November 1997?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am convinced there were none, but this was no longer my task. This was no longer my activity. Civilian organs of authority were in charge of that. If any such person had moved into the area - but I doubt it. I don't think that there were any in Tuzla or in the canton.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My -- I understand that, sir, my question is: In the 2nd Corps area of responsibility as it existed in 19 -- November 1997, outside of Tuzla and the Tuzla canton, were there any former members of the El Mujahedin Detachment living? I know you've said there were none in Tuzla, in the Tuzla canton. I'm talking about outside of Tuzla in the area covered by 2 Corps in November 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yeah, Your Honour -- Your Honour, I referred to -- to what the -- the question put to the witness was: Was there anyone living during or after the war in Tuzla and not in any region outside or canton outside? So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, can you say that again? Or let me read it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The point, Your Honour, is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'm objecting because it's going beyond the scope of the question put to the witness during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question -- the question that was originally put by my learned colleague, again on page 76, lines 18 to 21, implies that the 2nd Corps consisted exclusively of the Tuzla canton. My question simply is saying that there might be areas of the 2nd Corps responsibility in 1997 outside of Tuzla where former members of the El Mujahedin Detachment may have been living at that time, 1997, November 1997, which might go to the issue as to why this document may have been addressed to the 2nd Corps commander in late 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The objection is overruled. You may proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General Delic, do you understand the question that I'm asking you, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you, and I will answer. My area of responsibility remained the same, but I said that there had been a reorganisation in the ranks of the BiH army. The 3rd Corps, the 7th Corps, and the 4th Corps stopped existing as a result of that. Parts of the commands for development that had used to belong to the 3rd Corps were placed under my authority. I said that this was the area of Zavidovici, that this was the area of Tesanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, sorry, Mr. Delic. You know, we would like you to go home for the weekend. Please answer the question. You are not answering the question. The question is: Were there any El Mujahid members -- former members of the El Mujahid residing in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps outside Tuzla and Tuzla canton in November 1997? That is the question. Your answer should be "yes" or "no," because we -- we want to make sure that you go home. Unless you want to be here next week. You want to spend the weekend here, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I respect you and I would like to give you my answer, but it will be both "yes" and "no," that's why I would like to explain why "yes," why "no." No, because this was not my area of responsibility. Yes, because in Zavidovici there was a command for the development of the brigade which used to belong to the 3rd Corps of the BiH army, which at the relevant period was a development command. And in the municipality of Zavidovici in a place called Bocinja they had erected a village, a community of the Mujahedin. I know that they had put up their tents there. Nobody could come close to them. They were very close. They had bought some of the Serb houses. They were there illegally. It was not in my area of responsibility but it was in the area where my development command was. The area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps remained the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. I accepted those brigades because they had to be under somebody's authority. These people had to be under somebody's command and control after the transformation, and I believe that the Prosecutor now is happy with my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just try to make sure that we understand. Bocinja in Zavidovici municipality in November 1997 fell within which ARBiH corps area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3 Corps. 3 Corps, which we -- which was some sort of a command for development.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us earlier with this reorganisation that 3 Corps disappeared. Do you know when 3rd Corps was disbanded?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I don't even know whether this happened in 1997. I believe so. I'm just guessing. This is a guessing game. I know that those groups that had been part of that corps, the 7 became part of the 3rd Corps and then they returned to the 2nd Corps, only commands for development. I'm talking about 10 or 15 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, yesterday you told us this is Ramadan. You don't dare guess. Please don't guess. But apart from it being Ramadan, we don't want guesswork. We want what you know factually. So don't guess. If you don't know, just say you don't know. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions. Thank you.
