utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The French translation is now over. There is a lag and a difference between the French and the English version. And it's very difficult to follow the proceedings in French. Thank you. But to return on this document, what I understood - and I may be wrong - is that the fact that there is no signature -- no handwritten signature is not a real problem regarding this document, given that this is the document that was received at the receiving end through this packet transmission that you told us about.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the document being decoded, and that's why there is no handwritten signature. But I wonder whether it would be possible, whether in the deciphering process of the document that was sent through the packet system, there might not be the number of the protocol, which mainly would only appear in the original. Would that be possible, that that number would be only in the original?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may be right. Both on the original and the document that was received by packet communication, there should be such a heading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I have another question. In 1997, what function did General Rasim Delic occupy? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Army general Rasim Delic was the commander of the General Staff of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have a few more questions. You yesterday during the examination-in-chief, you talked about the chain which would go up to the 3rd Corps, to the 2nd Corps, so the command chain. And today, during the cross-examination, you talked about a chain that was going top to bottom from the Presidency all the way down to the field. And this was a chain that was used for orders. So I have a question on the command chain but dealing with omissions, and I would like to go from bottom up. So if there were illegal activities going on that would have been committed by soldiers or officers - and we're talking here at the bottom level - the commander of this lower unit, on the field, this -- I don't know what is the lowest unit that could be found. But commander of this unit, was he duty-bound to conduct his unit in a way to make sure that illegal activities would not be committed and if illegal activities were eventually committed, was he duty-bound to sanction these illegal activities?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, you are absolutely right. However, his competence, the competence of a commander, differs depending on the level. The actions that can be taken by the commanding officer at the lowest level, such as a squad or platoon, is not the same to that of the higher-up level, such as a company, battalion, or even further up, a brigade, which consists of several battalions, or even further up, a division, which consists of several brigades. What should I tell you? The lowest person should inform the lowest -- the low-ranking commander should inform his immediate superior, who in turn should -- should propose certain measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it goes up. It must go up. And if by chance someone who was duty-bound to make sure that nothing would happen or sanction in case something has happened does not do it, then his superior -- if his superior suddenly finds out that these activities have been going on, these illegal activities have been going on, he's still duty-bound to report -- or to prevent and sanction, at least. There's no interruption in the chain. Is that the way it works?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this goes all the way up. This is -- it goes all the way up. It applies to every single level; right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I see it. That's the logic of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I have another small question: Today you told us that in the 7th Muslim Brigade there were no Croats, no Croats from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am convinced that there weren't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So to your knowledge, were there any Serbs from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there were any Serbs either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this means that there were only Muslim Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And there were only those -- only Muslim Bosniaks, but were there also foreign Muslims? As far as you know.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, there were no Bosniaks, pure Bosniaks. And I mean those who were non-Muslims, such as atheists, for instance. I believe that they were all practicing Muslims Bosniaks there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And they were all local Muslims or were there foreign Muslims also?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was made up of local Bosniaks from Bosnia-Herzegovina, 100 per cent of it. There may have been Muslims from other parts of the former Yugoslavia there too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But no foreigners from abroad.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe there were no foreigners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you're not sure.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, unfortunately, I'm speculating, but I'm almost certain. Let's say 70 to 80 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. It is past time. We are going to have to adjourn, sir. You have to come back Monday morning, at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom II, to my knowledge. Court adjourned to Monday, the 24th of September, at 9.00 in the morning. Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
